title: SDK policy profiles: conservative/balanced/aggressive defaults, client-side budgets, and idempotency hints
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define and implement a set of opinionated client-side retry/backoff profile templates ("conservative", "balanced", "aggressive") across Python/TS/Go SDKs, paired with a small, backwards-compatible idempotency hint envelope and a runtime budget system. The goal is to provide safe defaults that reduce production retries, improve latency tail behavior, and make it straightforward for product teams to pick a profile or tune a per-route budget without deep infra changes.
acceptance_criteria: Three policy profiles implemented and documented in python/typescript/go SDKs: conservative, balanced, aggressive
Each profile maps to documented retry budget, max attempts, backoff curve, and error classifications
A lightweight idempotency hint envelope is supported by all SDKs and logged in telemetry (no server-side contract required)
Per-route client-configurable retry budgets are supported by SDK config and surfaced in Console telemetry
End-to-end examples (chat completion + streaming, embeddings, rerank) exist for each language and each profile
Integration tests simulate common transient failures and assert no accidental duplicate-apply for non-idempotent routes when conservative profile used
proposed_solution: Introduce "policy profiles" as first-class SDK presets. Each profile bundles: retryable-error categories, max_attempts, initial_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, backoff_multiplier, jitter_strategy, and a soft retry_budget token pool. SDKs will expose a per-client and per-route override API and emit standard telemetry events when budgets are consumed or budgets block retries. For idempotency, add an optional envelope field "idempotency_hint" which is opaque string generated by SDK helpers; servers may use it if available but no mandatory server behavior is required. For streams, include resume_token handling guidance and a small 'resume window' default for conservative profile. Provide cross-language reference implementation and migration guide from existing ad-hoc retry settings.
implementation_notes: Python: add new RetryPolicy class, expose client.policy = PolicyProfile.BALANCED
TS: add createClient({ policy: 'conservative' | 'balanced' | 'aggressive' }) factory, ensure browser and node parity
Go: implement profiles in clientopts and provide simple helper to wrap existing transport retry middleware
Telemetry: add events retry_attempt, retry_blocked_budget, idempotency_hint_sent with schema version header
Tests: fuzz with packet-loss simulator + 5s tail-latency bursts; validate no duplicate side-effects for conservative profile
Docs: quickstart snippet for each profile and a migration section titled 'Choosing a profile for production'
risks: Clients may rely on opaque idempotency_hint without server enforcement causing false sense of protection
Aggressive profile could increase cost and double-submit risk for edge-case non-idempotent endpoints
Telemetry explosion if we log every budget-consume event without sampling
Cross-language parity risk (behavior drift between SDKs) leading to hard-to-debug production differences
tests: Unit: policy parameter serialization, backoff math, jitter distribution checks
Integration: multi-attempt replay harness against a test server that fails first N requests with transient 502/503 and then succeeds
End-to-end: simulate streaming interruption and resume_token replay with conservative profile ensuring single-apply semantics
Load: validate budget accounting under high concurrency (client-side budgets don't leak tokens)
